_comment: WordPress + WooCommerce: cache rendered HTML pages only.
Rules are ordered and the FIRST match wins, including exclusions -
so every 'enabled: false' rule must come before the catch-all at the end.
Cookie names are matched against cookie NAMES only, never values.
Static assets. Apache already serves these efficiently with sendfile
and mod_expires, and they never reach PHP, so caching them buys
nothing and costs a cache lookup on every asset request - which is
most requests on a page. Excluded by path so the lookup is skipped
entirely; the catch-all's content_types is the backstop.

_comment: Any URL carrying a query string. '?*' means 'at least one character'.

preview nonces, and - importantly - tracking parameters: the query
is part of the cache key, so every distinct ?utm_source=... would
otherwise become its own entry and the cache would grow without
